lines.DL001: Did you touch the heat? The apartment just went from fall to the Sahara.
lines.DL002: I set it to seventy-two. That is a scientifically civilized temperature.
lines.DL003: My left foot says we have moved to the Arctic.
lines.DL004: Your left foot is wearing summer socks in November. It gets no vote.
lines.DL005: Then my right foot is requesting an independent second opinion.
lines.DL006: New rule: neither of us changes the thermostat without telling the other.
lines.DL007: Fine. Does leaving a written notice on the thermostat count?
lines.DL008: It means saying it out loud. With words. Ideally while looking at me.
lines.DL009: Understood. This is your official notice that I am turning it up.
lines.DL010: I asked for a warning, not a ceremonial act of provocation.
lines.DL011: I am not arguing. I am placing thermometers and trusting the data.
lines.DL012: Why is there a thermometer inside the coffee jar?
lines.DL013: It represents an important area of our daily morning activity.
lines.DL014: The coffee is a hundred and forty degrees. According to you, we live in a volcano.
lines.DL015: Good point. We should exclude all readings contaminated by caffeine.
lines.DL016: You also put a thermometer next to the oven while it was on.
lines.DL017: That is the positive control. Any serious experiment needs extremes.
lines.DL018: Your experiment proves the oven gets hot. Congratulations, Professor Winter.
lines.DL019: Let us vote. You want seventy, and I want seventy-four.
lines.DL020: There are only two of us. That is not democracy; that is a tie with radiators.
lines.DL021: The couch could cast a vote. It spends more time here than we do.
lines.DL022: The couch is upholstered. It will always vote for warmth. Clear conflict of interest.
lines.DL023: Then ask the plant. It has suffered through every argument.
lines.DL024: The plant is plastic. Its environmental credentials are questionable.
lines.DL025: We could run an algorithm to calculate a fair compromise.
lines.DL026: Halfway between seventy and seventy-four is seventy-two. We learned that yesterday.
lines.DL027: Yes, but yesterday we did not have an algorithm charging consulting fees.
lines.DL028: I designed three comfort zones: warm living room, neutral kitchen, cool bedroom.
lines.DL029: Why is there masking tape across the hallway?
lines.DL030: It marks the boundary between two microclimates. Do not cross without acclimating.
lines.DL031: Leo, the entire apartment uses the same heating system.
lines.DL032: That is why the borders are symbolic. They create a feeling of control.
lines.DL033: The tape is stuck to my slippers. Apparently I have dual citizenship.
lines.DL034: We could issue climate passports and stamp them at every border.
lines.DL035: Or we could make one simple rule: remove the tape.
lines.DL036: Fine. But the bedroom keeps its independence until the next summit.
lines.DL037: I built an app that records temperature and humidity every minute.
lines.DL038: Would it not be easier to put on a sweater when we feel cold?
lines.DL039: That does not scale. My system has charts and intelligent alerts.
lines.DL040: Then why did it just send me an extreme weather warning?
lines.DL041: The humidity sensor is sitting over a pot of boiling water.
lines.DL042: Your system thinks the kitchen is experiencing a monsoon.
lines.DL043: Then I will put a tiny umbrella over the sensor and correct the readings.
lines.DL044: Do not put an umbrella on a thermometer. Move it away from the pot.
lines.DL045: Logging an incident: operations management is resisting innovation.
lines.DL046: Your app says we spent thirty dollars on sensors.
lines.DL047: That is an investment. In the long run, we will save on heating.
lines.DL048: And how much money have we saved since this research began?
lines.DL049: We cannot measure that yet. The observation period is too short.
lines.DL050: You also bought a tablet just to look at temperature readings.
lines.DL051: It was essential. My phone gave me too narrow a perspective.
lines.DL052: For that money we could have kept this place warm all week.
lines.DL053: True, but then we would not have all this valuable information.
lines.DL054: Our main findings are that we are cold and have less money.
lines.DL055: Let us try something radical: turn off the screens and share a blanket.
lines.DL056: Agreed, as long as we record the temperature before and after.
lines.DL057: It is a plaid blanket. It does not need a performance dashboard.
lines.DL058: I want to prove that a simple solution can beat a complex one.
lines.DL059: Beautiful thought, considering it took you three days to reach it.
lines.DL060: Not three days. Forty-eight hours and nine minutes, technically.
lines.DL061: Now you are timing how long you have been defending a blanket.
lines.DL062: For once, that is actually useful information from my research.
lines.DL063: Then write down the conclusion: Vera was right this time.
lines.DL064: Maybe you are right. I turned a single degree into a border dispute.
lines.DL065: And I defended the thermostat like it was a national monument.
lines.DL066: Peace treaty: seventy-two degrees, and everyone may wear sweaters.
lines.DL067: On one condition: the plant never gets another vote.
lines.DL068: Deal. And somehow, it finally feels warmer in here.
lines.DL069: Wait. Why is the curtain moving if every door is closed?
lines.DL070: The window is open a crack. I opened it to air the room this morning.
lines.DL071: We argued for two hours because you left a window open?
lines.DL072: Not exactly. We made huge progress in teamwork and science.
lines.DL073: I will close the window. You are going to unplug those sensors.
lines.DL074: Fair. But I want to keep the final chart as a souvenir.
lines.DL075: Keep it. Just do not turn it into a family presentation.
lines.DL076: What about one slide on lessons learned and common mistakes?
lines.DL077: Slide one: an open window in November.
lines.DL078: Slide two: two adults who would rather debate than check.
lines.DL079: Slide three: we can still laugh at ourselves.
lines.DL080: I like that one. I might add a picture of us under the blanket.
lines.DL081: Fine, as long as I do not need a password to open the picture.
lines.DL082: Done. Window closed, heat stable, sensors unplugged.
lines.DL083: This is wonderful. I forgot how peaceful not measuring anything can be.
lines.DL084: Even the plant looks happier. And it does not have an opinion.
lines.DL085: I put up a sign: independent and happy climate zone.
lines.DL086: Did we not agree to stop founding countries inside the apartment?
lines.DL087: It is a tiny vegetable republic. No budget or government employees.
lines.DL088: Tomorrow you will build customs and charge me taxes for watering it.
lines.DL089: Do not be ridiculous. I was saving customs for the socks.
lines.DL090: Come here, Minister of Winter. I am confiscating a blanket.
